benefit_context.instructions: Inspect the whole background for source-supported potential benefits applicable to this study, even when risks_benefits.benefits is empty. Return benefit_interpretation with potential_benefits (source_path/source_excerpt exact quotation pairs) and rationale. Preserve each applicable qualified possibility in this section, with uncertainty and no guarantee of personal benefit. Historical evidence about other studies or treatments is context, not proof of this study's benefit; never turn a hypothetical advantage into an established result. Retrospective record review must not promise treatment benefit. If no applicable benefit is stated, return an empty list and explain why; use authorized fallback wording without inventing a benefit or requesting optional input.

fixed_boilerplate.text: Applicable ethics review requirements and ethical and privacy protections govern study conduct.

content_expectations: Identify the designated ethics review body and preserve the explicit current approval, exemption and waiver status, including not submitted or not granted. A future obligation to obtain approval does not replace current status. Preserve supplied participant-impact facts, including any absence of direct benefit, compensation terms, and how research-related concerns are reported. Do not invent a waiver, injury-care payment, or additional oversight policy.
Do not replace supplied detail with generic clinical prose.

constraints: The Source-of-Truth is approved and source intake is closed. Do not request additional reviewer input.

Use only supplied approved evidence and applicable template/Fixed Clinical Boilerplate. Align shared population, groups, quantities, timing, procedures and outcomes across the Protocol, selected ICF and PRS narratives; preserve relationships and qualifications rather than copying wording.

Listed Fixed Clinical Boilerplate is authorized only where applicable and consistent with the approved source. The approved source supersedes boilerplate; boilerplate must not expand decision-making authority, termination grounds, completion criteria, procedures, or safety obligations.

When a section lists both Fixed Clinical Boilerplate and minimum evidence, include all material source facts and only applicable, nonconflicting boilerplate; omit boilerplate clauses that would alter a source rule.

Do not invent study-specific facts, procedures, risks, benefits, safety obligations, legal promises, or regulatory claims. Routine-use and record-review studies acquire no additional visits, monitoring or follow-up commitments from boilerplate.
Preserve supplied numbered citations next to the Protocol claims they support and their bibliography linkage. Do not invent citations; ICF explanations use plain language.
Return exactly one result for every requested section ID.
Use only the drafted or fixed_boilerplate outcome. Sparse sections may use only applicable, source-consistent listed Fixed Clinical Boilerplate.
Return structured section content, not a whole document or document markup.

Write to each section's purpose and ownership. Explain each operational rule fully in its owning section; elsewhere give only the fact needed for that section and a brief reference to the owning heading. Preserve necessary identifiers, endpoint definitions, quantities, timing anchors/windows, conditions, exceptions, safety information and client consent language. Compress repeated explanations, not clinical meaning.
Use participant-facing language for ICF sections.

writing_examples illustrate prose and organization using synthetic inputs. Draft from this request's approved_source and section_contracts; example facts are never study evidence or boilerplate. Return the requested response format.
For icf.key-information-summary, draft directly from its canonical summary obligations; keep each concept concise and never copy a complete detailed-section sentence or paragraph.

For a Sterling ICF, BACKGROUND owns lens descriptions, comparative evidence, the evidence gap, and rationale. PURPOSE must be concise and limited to the purpose, hypothesis, and primary endpoint; do not restate BACKGROUND.

Endpoint names, visit names and timing, identifiers, quantities, safety terms, and brief traceability cross-references may recur.

Use protocol_writing_plan for the active Protocol headings and method/completion owners. General Information is a compact synopsis; Objectives states purpose; Study Design owns comparisons and endpoints; Bias explains why controls matter. Place full operational rules in the named active methods_owner and completion rules in completion_owner, even when their heading differs by branch. Statistical Methodology owns calculations/models. Cross-reference only a heading listed in the plan. When assessment_table_owner is null, describe the historical windows and activities in prose or lists rather than claiming a matrix or columns are rendered.

Satisfy every section's content_expectations and cover every material value named by minimum_evidence. If the writing plan names an assessment_table_owner, its source-derived table and notes carry that inventory and adjacent prose only introduces it. Otherwise the active methods_owner carries the full historical assessment details in prose or lists.

Write standalone clinical content that serves the section purpose. Refer to the study and its procedures directly, rather than to the synopsis, approved source, or drafting process. Preserve genuine numbered instruments/forms, citations and explained footnotes; remove a suspected orphan marker only when its source context supports that interpretation. Omit self-referential filler and redundant narration. These editorial preferences are not publication gates.

Use reference_detail_target_words only as a soft compression signal; independent AI review assesses substantive completeness, and concise complete prose must not be padded, repeated, or invented to meet a length target.
Explicitly distinguish the study objective, hypothesis, and endpoints when they describe different constructs.
When the approved source does not define an instrument, scoring rule, denominator, missing-data method, date, or version, do not invent one or expose an internal source-gap note.
Do not use an evidence reference unless the returned prose or list actually contains the material fact it supports.

Every paragraph object and every list object must include at least one evidence_refs or boilerplate_refs value allowed by its section contract. If prose only introduces an already-cited list, omit that paragraph instead of returning empty reference arrays.

=### Context:
We are writing a clinical retrospective study protocol document.  
Your task is to generate the **Statistics & Sample Size** sections.  


### Inputs we will provide:
- Study Title: The full official title of the study.  
- Study Design: Free text describing the study design as provided in the form.  
- Primary Objective: The main study objective.
- Key Endpoints: The list of primary and secondary endpoints.
- Inclusion Criteria: To identify the pathologies being treated.
- Sample Size: The planned sample size and its justification.
- Statistical Analysis Plan: Free text describing the planned statistical methods. 


### What you need to do:
- Generate **sampleSizeJustification**: a formal justification paragraph using the provided rationale.  

- Generate **analysisDataSets**: a short introductory paragraph for section **9.1 Analysis Data Sets**, describing the data sources reviewed and the overall scope of data collection.  
This paragraph must NOT include bullet points.
- Generate **analysisDataSetsBullets**: a bullet-point list of key variables and endpoints analyzed in section **9.1**, using the bullet character `• `.  
Each bullet must include:
  · The variable or endpoint name 
  · A brief description of how it is measured or derived  
  · Yes/No definitions where applicable  
Do not include introductory or closing sentences in this field.
- Generate **statisticalMethodology**: structured description of statistical methods for primary and secondary endpoints.  
- Generate **statisticalConsiderations**: general considerations (software, significance level, handling of missing data, multiplicity, etc.). 

### Important notes:
- Do not invent numbers or tests not provided.  
- Keep the writing formal and professional, consistent with clinical protocol standards.  


### Output format:
Return only valid JSON in the following structure:
{
  "sampleSizeJustification": "formal justification paragraph",
  "analysisDataSets": "description of safety/efficacy datasets",
  "analysisDataSetsBullets": "• bullet 1\n• bullet 2...",
  "statisticalMethodology": "detailed description of statistical methods",
  "statisticalConsiderations": "considerations such as software, significance level, missing data",
}

=### Study Title:
A Randomized, Single-Masked, Contralateral Eye Study of Active Sentry Versus Ozil in Cataract Surgery

### Study Design:
Single site, randomized, prospective contralateral eye study. Each subject will undergo sequential bilateral uncomplicated cataract surgery, with one eye randomized to Active Sentry at low IOP and the other to Ozil at high IOP.

### Primary Objective:
To assess the efficiency of the Active Sentry handpiece at low intraocular pressure compared with the Ozil handpiece at high intraocular pressure.

### Key Endpoints:
- Primary Endpoints: Total aspiration time (seconds).
- Secondary Endpoints: Cumulative Dissipated Energy (CDE), total fluid used (mL), and incidence of intraoperative complications (e.g., posterior capsule rupture).
- Safety Endpoint: Change in corneal endothelial cell count at 3 months.

### Inclusion Criteria:
- Adult patients (≥ 18 years) with bilateral, stable, and uncomplicated age-related cataracts.
- Patients planned for sequential bilateral phacoemulsification with IOL implantation.

### Sample Size:
Sample Size: 70 eyes of 35 subjects. Justification: Assuming a pooled standard deviation of 36.85 seconds and a mean difference of 0 seconds, the study would require 32 eyes per group (64 total) to achieve 80% power at a two-sided alpha of 0.05, with a non-inferiority margin of 23 seconds. To account for potential dropouts, 70 eyes of 35 subjects will be enrolled.

### Statistical Analysis Plan: 
Safety analysis will include all subjects enrolled. Efficacy analysis will be limited to eyes that completed uncomplicated cataract surgery. For continuous variables, data summaries will include sample size, mean, standard deviation, median, minimum, and maximum. For categorical variables, summaries will report number and percentage of subjects in each category. The difference in aspiration time between groups will be tested for non-inferiority. Non-inferiority will be concluded if the upper bound of the 95% confidence interval is ≤23 seconds; if met, a superiority test will follow. Statistical analyses will be conducted using R (version 4.1.2 or higher), with alpha = 0.05.

={
  "sampleSizeJustification": "Assuming a pooled standard deviation of 36.85 seconds and a mean difference of 0 seconds, the study would require a sample size of 32 for each group (i.e., 64 eyes of 32 subjects) to achieve a power of 80% and a level of significance of 5% ($ \alpha = 0.05 $) for declaring that the Active Sentry handpiece is not inferior to the Ozil at a 23-second margin of non-inferiority. To account for potential dropouts and ensure statistical robustness, a total of 35 subjects (70 eyes) will be recruited for enrollment.",
  "analysisDataSets": "All subjects enrolled in the study will be evaluated for safety. Efficacy analyses will be performed based on data from those eyes where uncomplicated cataract surgery was successfully completed. Recorded surgical logs from the phacoemulsification systems and patient medical records will be reviewed. The completed electronic data set will be used for all subsequent analyses.",
  "analysisDataSetsBullets": "• Total Aspiration Time: Measured in seconds from the initiation of phacoemulsification to completion, recorded via surgical system logs.\n• Cumulative Dissipated Energy (CDE): Total energy delivered during surgery, recorded from the surgical system parameters.\n• Total Fluid Used: Volume of irrigation fluid in milliliters (mL), recorded from medical records and system logs.\n• Surgical Success: Determined at the conclusion of the procedure. Success = 'Yes' if uncomplicated phacoemulsification and IOL implantation are achieved; 'No' if any intraoperative complication (e.g., posterior capsule rupture) occurs.\n• Endothelial Cell Count: Measured via specular microscopy pre-operatively and at 3 months, recorded from medical records.",
  "statisticalMethodology": "A descriptive summary of the data will be prepared for all measurement timepoints. For continuous variables (e.g., aspiration time, CDE), summaries will include sample size, mean, standard deviation, median, minimum, and maximum. For categorical variables, summaries will report the number and percentage of subjects in each category. The difference in aspiration time between groups will be used to test the non-inferiority hypothesis. If the upper boundary of the 95% confidence interval is $\le 23$ seconds, non-inferiority will be concluded. If non-inferiority is demonstrated, a subsequent test of superiority will be performed.", 
  "statisticalConsiderations": "All statistical analyses will be performed using R, version 4.1.2 or higher. Any statistical tests of hypotheses will employ a level of significance of $ \alpha = 0.05 $. Multiplicity will be controlled via the predefined step-down testing approach for secondary endpoints. No data imputation will be performed for missing values unless a specific sensitivity analysis is required."
}

adapter_instructions: For each mapped target, use its retained n8n messages as the base writing prompt. Produce only the named legacy field's content for that native section.

Return the current request's section_results or narrative schema, identifiers and evidence references. The old JSON aliases and section numbers are transport examples; the current template owns headings, numbering, tables and formatting.

A list group may contain a nonempty label alongside items. That label renders as an unbulleted paragraph immediately before the group's items; use it to separate endpoint categories without turning introductions into bullets.

This experiment checks response bindings, section inventory and text/list shape only. Evidence references may be retained for manual inspection; schedule_interpretation, benefit_interpretation and assessment_presentation bookkeeping is optional. The source-derived table is built directly from approved source rows.

Approved source facts and current section content_expectations (including Brad's corrections) override conflicting legacy instructions and demonstrations. Demonstration studies are examples, never evidence for this study.

Apply editorial_corrections only to their named target sections. They refine the retained n8n writing prompts; supplied study facts and applicable client consent language remain authoritative. Missing optional source detail is not a reason to expand or invent clinical content.

Use protocol_writing_plan and the current section ownership instructions to tighten the retained prompts: keep Protocol synopses brief, explain each operational rule fully in its owning section and use brief heading references elsewhere. Endpoint definitions and analysis calculations remain complete where needed; ICF explanations remain self-contained for participants. Preserve every material quantity, window, exception and safety qualification.

Write final study prose, not commentary about drafting. Translate source directions into the applicable study fact: for example, 'Day 30 ratings are descriptive only' rather than an explanation about inventing registry outcomes. Omit empty category labels when no endpoint belongs to that category.

For evaluation-procedures, inspect the supplied assessment_presentation notes against the approved table. When an edit is needed, return the existing source_text/display_text/rationale shape to retain unique information without repeating the matrix. This is part of drafting, not a separate review task.

For ICF requests also follow consent_template_comments. Assess applicability from the approved source and selected family, preserving supplied conditions and existing family-owned sections. Template comments do not establish new study facts or authorization.

Use only the approved comparator, endpoints, visits, risks, benefits, statistical methods and regulatory facts. Omit legacy defaults that invent placebo, standard-of-care comparators, extra outcomes, inferred side-effect lists, dates or significance levels.
For current_instruction_targets, draft study-specific content from the approved source and current section instructions, retaining applicable fixed client language.

The current source-derived tables, short-title/header formatting and PRS structural builder remain authoritative. This experiment stops at unreviewed native files; it requires no independent review or repair responses.
